title: Completion of a Clean Call
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $\mathrm{emit}$ be a Boolean mode, and let $x$, $\mathrm{arg}$, and $\mathrm{cap}$ be Boolean words. If $M$ halts on input $\mathrm{arg}$ with output $\mathrm{cap}$ after $T$ steps, then the call machine for $M$ in mode $\mathrm{emit}$, started on physical input $x$ with $\mathrm{arg}$ on its first work tape and all other work tapes blank, reaches after some $t \le (24+13k)(T+|\mathrm{arg}|+|\mathrm{cap}|+1)$ steps the configuration with exit state $5$, with $\mathrm{arg}$ on the first work tape when $\mathrm{emit}$ is true and $\mathrm{cap}$ there otherwise, all other work tapes blank, and output $\mathrm{cap}$ when $\mathrm{emit}$ is true and empty otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite-state Boolean Turing machine with k work tapes
x, arg, and cap are Boolean words
M halts on arg with output cap after T steps
replaced:
Let $M$ be a machine with $k$ work tapes computing output $c$ on argument $a$ within
time $T$. For every mode and input word, there is a time $t \le (24 + 13k)(T + |a| + |c|
+ 1)$ such that the clean-call controller, run for $t$ steps from its canonical entry
seam on $a$, reaches the canonical exit seam carrying $c$ in install mode and $a$ in
emit mode, with output $c$ exactly in emit mode.
